messages:
sara: Quick sync: who should enforce per-tenant admission controls (rate limits, model routing, feature flags) when requests traverse Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private variants?

ben: My initial take: enforcement should live as close to the runtime as possible for latency and fail-open semantics. Control plane can assert desired policy but runtime must be the source of truth at enforcement time.

diego: Agree on latency, but remember dedicated pools are multi-tenant in our infra. If we push enforcement solely to runtime, ops loses a central visibility point for global quota burn.

elaine: Proposal: two-layer model. Control plane expresses policies as immutable manifests (policy_id, version, constraints) and the runtime fetches them and enforces locally. That gives central intent + local enforcement.

sara: Sounds reasonable. What about Private installs that disable control-plane egress?

ben: For Private w/ no egress we should support an operator-applied policy bundle during install and an on-prem agent for updates. Basically: manifest can be delivered via three channels: hosted push, runtime pull, or operator-apply.

infra-bot: Policy schema v1 draft ready at git.redwood/infra/policies/schema.yaml. Lint: warning: authz fields optional.

diego: Important tradeoffs to list:
- Consistency: push vs pull leads to different staleness windows.
- Survivability: runtime-only enforcement supports disconnected operation.
- Auditability: central control plane provides better observability for SLA and billing.

elaine: Implementation detail: runtime should keep policy revision (policy_id + seq). Enforce last-applied-seq and expose enforcement metrics. If control plane sends newer seq, runtime hot swaps the ruleset atomically.

sara: How do we handle ephemeral overrides? Example: emergency throttle for a rogue tenant during rollout.

ben: Add an override channel with explicit TTL. Overrides are higher priority but must be signed and have a clear audit trail and automatic expiry. For Private installs, overrides would be operator-only.

diego: Edge case: model-routing changes mid-request (can happen with streaming). We need a read-only policy check path in the runtime admission stage before token consumption to lock the routing decision.

elaine: Agree. Admission flow sketch:
```
1) ingress: authn/authz -> tenant resolved
2) admission: policy_check(tenant, route_hint, model_id) -> permit|deny|override
3) dispatch: router chooses host based on admission outcome
4) runtime enforces local per-token quotas and streaming limits
```

sara: For observability we should add per-tenant enforcement counters: denied_count, override_count, last_policy_seq, policy_staleness_seconds. Also emit policy_source (controlplane/pull/operator).

infra-bot: Note: storage requirements for last-applied policies retained for 90 days for audits.

ben: Security: manifests must be signed with our signing key and verified by runtime. For operator-applied bundles, require a separate operator key. We should document key rotation.

diego: Operational concern: if runtime applies policy that was meant for a different hosting mode (e.g., a Hosted-only quota change applied to Private), runtime must validate capability compatibility and reject with clear error. Include an allowed_hosting_modes list in the manifest.

elaine: Also add a compatibility matrix field to help the control plane avoid sending incompatible policies. Example: "allowed_hosting_modes": ["hosted","dedicated"].

sara: What about rollout semantics? Control plane wants to TTL/gradually apply policies (canary percentages). Do we support partial enforcement?

ben: We can support canary by attaching selectors in the manifest (percentage hash on tenant id or explicit tenant list). Runtime evaluates selector deterministically. For Dedicated, selectors may map to pools.

diego: Test matrix to add:
- policy hot-swap atomicity under heavy load
- override TTL expiry behavior
- offline operator-apply path + key rotation
- cross-hosting incompatibility rejection

elaine: I'll add the manifest schema snippet to the RFC branch. Example manifest snippet:
```
policy_id: quota-2026-03
seq: 17
allowed_hosting_modes: ["hosted","dedicated"]
selector: { type: "hash_pct", field: "tenant_id", pct: 5 }
rules: [ {type: "qps", limit: 10} ]
signature: "..."
```

sara: Next actions: ben drafts enforcement API and runtime hooks, diego writes tests, elaine updates RFC with schema and migration notes. Aim to have RFC addendum by next Wed.

infra-bot: CI check: branch feature/policy-manifest-hooks exists. Unit tests: 42 passed, 1 flaky.

sara: Thanks everyone. One small ask: include examples for Private install docs showing operator-apply and agent update.

ben: Will do.

diego: I'll own the canary selector impl and test vectors.

elaine: I'll add observability dashboards mock and log format.

sara: Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
